Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:1.hebrew: שני חצאי סימנין - פסול, דכמו דלא עביד מידי דמי, דזיל הכא ליכא שיעורא וזיל הכא ליכא שיעורא:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:1.english: Two halves of the [two] signs - It is invalid, for it is as if he had done nothing, since if you go here [to the windpipe], there is no [sufficient] measure, and if you go there [to the gullet], there is no [sufficient] measure.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:2.hebrew: בעוף - שצולהו כולו כאחד, וצריך שיוציא דמו בשחיטה יפה:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:2.english: In the case of a bird - For one roasts it whole, all together, and therefore it is necessary that it expel its blood through a proper slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:3.english: Until he slaughters, etc. - And the first Tanna disagrees only regarding the veins:

Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:4.hebrew: משום דושט סמוך לוורידין - נקט ליה, ומיהו הוא הדין לקנה. הוושט הוי בין קנה למפרקת, סמוך לוורידין:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:10:4.english: Because the gullet is adjacent to the veins - [The Gemara] mentioned it [the gullet], but nevertheless the same is true of the windpipe. The gullet is between the windpipe and the neck-vertebra, adjacent to the veins.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:11:1.hebrew: ושהה בה כו' כשרה - משום דחצי גרגרת לאו התחלת שחיטה היא, שאפילו נקרע חציו לא מיטרפא בהכי:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:11:1.english: And he paused in it, etc., it is valid - Because half of the windpipe is not the beginning of slaughter, as even if half of it were torn, [the animal] would not become a *tereifa* through this.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:11:2.hebrew: לא בבהמה - כלומר, הא אפילו בבהמה קאמר, דהא גמרה לאו אגרגרת קאי, אלא אכולה שחיטה קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:11:2.english: Not in an animal - That is to say, [the baraita] is speaking even about an animal, for [the phrase] "he completed it" does not refer to the windpipe, but rather refers to the entire act of slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:12:1.hebrew: וגמרו - סלקא דעתין, וגמרו בהאי כל שהוא, שהרי נשחט הרוב, דפגימה קמייתא כשלימה דמיא, והאיכא רוב קמן:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:12:1.english: And he completed it - It would enter one's mind [to say] that he completed it with this small amount [and so the slaughter is valid], since the majority has been slaughtered, for the first notch is considered like a whole [cut], and so there is a majority before us.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:1:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בעוף - קאי, שהרי דמו ראוי ליניכא לתולעת הגדלה בבגדי צמר שקורין טיני"א, כדכתיב "כבגד אכלו עש", וקאמר נוחרו ויפטר מן הכסוי. ואי אין שחיטה לעוף, נוחרו צריך כסוי, שזו היא שחיטתו:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:1:1.english: What, is it not about a bird - It does refer [to a bird], for its blood is fit to remove the worm that grows in woolen garments, which is called "tinia" (moth), as it is written, "like a garment eaten by a moth." And [the baraita] says that if he pierced it (*nochro*), he is exempt from covering [the blood]. But if there is no [Torah-law requirement of] slaughter for a bird, then if he pierced it, it should require covering, for this [piercing] is its slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:1:2.hebrew: ללכא - צבע עור אדום, שקורין פרק"א:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:1:2.english: Lalkha - A red skin dye, which [in Old French] is called "parque."

Rashi on Chullin 28a:2:1.hebrew: מלק - עוף קדשים בסכין, נבילה, דאין מליקה אלא בציפורן:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:2:1.english: He pinched [the neck] - A sacred bird, with a knife, [it is] an unslaughtered carcass (neveilah), as there is no pinching [melikah] except with the fingernail.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:2:2.hebrew: נהי נמי [דכי תבר] שדרה ומפרקת - בלא רוב בשר, כדאמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל חולין דף כא.), הויא טרפה, משום דסכין לאו מליקה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:2:2.english: Granted also that [when he breaks] the spine and the neck - Without [cutting] most of the flesh, as we said in the first chapter (above, Chullin 21a), it is a *tereifa*, because a knife is not [a valid method of] *melika*.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:2:3.english: Let a knife benefit it - That he [the slaughterer] cuts the signs [the windpipe and the gullet] after it had become a tereifa (an animal with a fatal defect).

Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:1.hebrew: הוא דאמר - רבי יצחק בן פנחס, דאמר כי האי תנא: עוף אין לו שחיטה, וכו':
Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:1.english: He who said - Rabbi Yitzchak ben Pinchas, who said like this Tanna: A bird has no [Torah-mandated] slaughter, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:2.english: Berabbi - [Rabbi Elazar HaKappar was] the greatest of his generation:

Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:3.hebrew: אך כאשר יאכל וגו' - בפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו במומן קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:3.english: "But as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, etc." - This refers to disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed on account of their blemish:

Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:4.hebrew: מה למדנו מצבי ואיל - הכי לכתוב: אך הטמא והטהור יחדו יאכלנו:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:3:4.english: What did we learn from the gazelle and the deer? - Thus [the verse] should have written: "But the impure and the pure may eat it together."

Rashi on Chullin 28a:4:1.hebrew: מה פסולי המוקדשין בשחיטה - דלעיל מההוא קרא כתיב: וזבחת מבקרך וגו'. בספרי גרסינן: מקיש צבי ואיל לבהמה, מה בהמה בשחיטה כו'. ולא מוקי להאי קרא דכי ירחיב בפסולי המוקדשין, אלא בבשר תאוה של חולין:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:4:1.english: Just as disqualified consecrated animals [require] slaughter - For above, from that verse, it is written: "And you shall slaughter from your herd, etc." In the Sifrei we read: It equates the deer and the gazelle to a domesticated animal: just as a domesticated animal [requires] slaughter, etc. And [the Sifrei] does not interpret this verse, "When [the Lord your God] will broaden [your border]" as referring to disqualified consecrated animals, but only to the meat of desire of unconsecrated animals.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:1.hebrew: מאן תנא - דלעיל, דקתני "נוחרו או עוקרו", דפליג עליה דרבי אלעזר הקפר:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:1.english: Who is the Tanna - [Who is the Tanna] above, who taught "if he gouged it or uprooted it," who disagrees with Rabbi Elazar HaKappar?

Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:2.hebrew: כאשר צויתיך - למד שנתפרשה לו מצות שחיטה על פה, דהיכן ציוהו בכתב:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:2.english: As I have commanded you - [Scripture] teaches that the commandment of slaughter was explained to him orally, for where did He command him in writing?

Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:3.hebrew: רוב אחד כו' - לאו מקרא יליף, אלא כלומר על הלכות שחיטה נצטוה:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:5:3.english: The majority of one [organ], etc. - He does not derive it from a verse; rather, the meaning is that he was commanded concerning the laws of slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:6:1.hebrew: וושט - מיוחד שבסימנים, הוא שחיות הבהמה תלוי בו, דהא בנקב במשהו מיטרפא, ואילו קנה, עד דמיפסק רובא:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:6:1.english: The esophagus - It is the most distinctive of the signs, in that the animal's life depends on it, for with a puncture of any size it becomes a *tereifa*, whereas [with] the windpipe, [it does not become a *tereifa*] unless most of it is severed.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:8:1.english: If he slaughtered the esophagus - In the case of a bird:

Rashi on Chullin 28a:8:2.hebrew: ואילו שחיטה בגרגרת לא קתני - דנימא שחט גרגרת ואח"כ נשמט הוושט, כשרה, אלמא לא מיתכשרא בקנה לחודיה:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:8:2.english: But slaughter at the windpipe he did not teach - So that we could say: If one slaughtered the windpipe and afterward the gullet slipped away, it is valid. Evidently, [the bird] is not rendered valid through the windpipe alone.

Rashi on Chullin 28a:9:1.hebrew: משום דגרגרת עבידא לאשתמוטי - להכי נקט שחיטה בוושט והשמטה בגרגרת:
Rashi on Chullin 28a:9:1.english: Because the windpipe is prone to slip away - Therefore [the baraita] specified slaughter with regard to the gullet, and slipping away with regard to the windpipe.

Tosafot on Chullin 28a:2:1.hebrew: תיהני לה סכין לטהרה מידי נבלה - הך פירכא ליתא לר' יוסי, דאמר בזבחים פרק חטאת העוף (זבחים דף סט:) גבי מלק ונמצאת טרפה, דאין מליקה מטהרת מידי נבלה, דדווקא שחיטה מטהרת בבהמה. אלא לרבי מאיר פריך, דקאמר התם נמי דמליקה מטהרת:
Tosafot on Chullin 28a:2:1.english: Let the knife be of benefit to it, to purify it from the status of neveilah - This refutation does not apply according to R. Yose, who said in Zevachim, in the chapter [beginning] "Chatat ha-Of" (Zevachim 69b), regarding [a bird] that was killed by melikah and was found to be a treifah, that melikah does not purify from the status of neveilah, for specifically shechitah purifies in the case of an animal. Rather, [the Gemara] is refuting [the matter] according to R. Meir, who says there as well that melikah does purify.

Tosafot on Chullin 28a:5:2.hebrew: ועל רוב אחד בעוף ועל רוב שנים בבהמה - י"מ דדריש בגימטריא דכאשר: אל"ף, אחד בעוף; שי"ן, שנים בבהמה; רי"ש, רובו של אחד כמוהו, רוב אחד בעוף ורוב שנים בבהמה. ראשי תיבות למפרע של כאשר הוי רובו של אחד כמוהו:
Tosafot on Chullin 28a:5:2.english: And [the verse refers] to the majority of one in a bird and to the majority of two in an animal - Some explain that [the Tanna] derives [this] through a letter-based exposition (gimatriya) of [the word] "ka'asher" ("as" [I have commanded you]): the alef [stands for] "one" in a bird; the shin [stands for] "two" in an animal; [and] the resh [stands for] "the majority of one is like it [the whole]" (rovo shel echad kamohu), [meaning] the majority of one in a bird and the majority of two in an animal. [For] the initial letters of "rovo shel echad kamohu," in reverse order, make up the word "ka'asher."
